module: Third-party LuaSocket library (Diego Nehab), version "URL 1.0.3": parsing, building and resolving relative URLs according to RFC 2396. Useful for splitting a URL into scheme/authority/userinfo/host/port/path/params/query/fragment, rebuilding it, encoding/decoding reserved characters (%XX) and handling path segments.
usage:
local url = require('socket.url')
local p = url.parse('http://user:pw@example.com:8080/a/b;p?x=1#frag')
print(p.host, p.port, p.path, p.query)  -- example.com 8080 /a/b x=1
print(url.absolute('http://example.com/a/b', '../c'))
notes: The module is declared locally (`_M`); the file is loaded via `require` from the code that needs it.
`parse` returns nil and "invalid url" for an empty string; the IPv6 authority in brackets is recognized (host without the brackets).
The comment of `unescape` in the source is a copy of that of `escape`: `unescape` does decode the %XX sequences.

escape.desc: Encodes a binary string by replacing each non-alphanumeric byte with its %XX representation.

unescape.desc: Decodes the %XX sequences of a string into bytes.

parse.desc: Splits a URL into a table with the fields scheme, authority, userinfo, user, password, host, port, path, params, query, fragment (only those present are filled). The leading '/' of the path is part of path.

default.desc: Default values copied into the result before parsing.

returns.desc: URL parts, or nil and "invalid url".

build.desc: Rebuilds a URL from a table of the type returned by parse; components containing reserved characters are protected.

absolute.desc: Builds an absolute URL from a base URL and a relative URL (RFC 2396).

base_url.desc: Base URL (string or table from parse).

relative_url.desc: Relative URL (string or table from parse).

parse_path.desc: Splits a path into (decoded) segments; a path starting with '/' gives an is_absolute field.

build_path.desc: Rebuilds a path from its segments, escaping protected characters.

unsafe.desc: If true, the segments are not protected before building.
